summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: This bill would push back the date by which the Parliamentary Budget Office must publish its post-election report on the cost of parties' promises.
It would amend the Parliamentary Service Act 1999 to give the PBO more time to prepare the report after a federal election.

The change follows a 2017 independent review that also recommended expanding the report to include medium-term financial impacts and policies of smaller parties, but those changes do not need legislation.
changes: The bill changes the deadline for publishing the post-election report.
It amends the Parliamentary Service Act 1999 to allow more time for the report's preparation.
The delayed publication is intended to accommodate the expanded scope of the report and to increase its visibility closer to when Parliament resumes.
summary.affected: The Parliamentary Budget Office and political parties with five or more parliamentarians are affected, as well as smaller parties that choose to be included in the report.

speeches.speaker: Alex Hawke
speeches.brief: The bill amends the Parliamentary Service Act to delay the release of the Parliamentary Budget Office's post-election report on election commitments, allowing more time to include medium-term financial impacts and policies from parties with fewer than five members, and to improve visibility by timing it closer to the resumption of parliament.

speeches.speaker: Andrew Leigh
speeches.brief: Labor will support the Parliamentary Service Amendment (Post-election Report) Bill 2018, extending the deadline for the Parliamentary Budget Office’s post-election report to either 30 days after the caretaker period or seven days before the first sitting day, whichever is later. The speaker also argued that the Abbott-Turnbull-Morrison government has mismanaged the budget, accruing over half of Australia’s $360 billion net debt, and noted that Labor established the Parliamentary Budget Office to provide independent, non-partisan policy costings.

speeches.speaker: Greg Hunt
speeches.brief: The Parliamentary Service Amendment (Post-Election Report) Bill was argued to extend the timeframe and scope for the Parliamentary Budget Office’s post-election report, allowing inclusion of medium-term financial impacts and policies from parties with fewer than five members. The speaker thanked the Prime Minister, Treasurer and finance minister, and claimed the government inherited a fiscal black hole in 1996 and a structural deficit in 2013, but has brought the budget back to surplus.
